params.body:
A new page, **Netwerk** (`/netwerk`), for the workshop of 16 October. Both parts of the questionnaire start from a graph on screen: GLK's network of relations, clustered and weighed for handing it over, and the road from request to order. This builds both from Bouwsoft and lets the facilitators note per relation what the table says.

## What comes in from Bouwsoft (read only, `relations:sync`)

Over the last three years (`NETWORK_YEARS`), by column, so nothing else leaves Bouwsoft:

- **Addresses**: name, place, Bouwsoft's own grouping, whether it is a client and/or a supplier there, and when it was created. No phone, email, IBAN or VAT number.
- **Orders**: as client per project, with the document type (quote, order, ...), its date and whether and when it was approved or rejected. No amounts.
- **SalesInvoices**: as client per project, with the date.
- **PurchaseInvoiceProjects** (with the date from **PurchaseInvoices**): as supplier per project, with the cost category. No amounts.
- **ProjectContacts**: as contact on a project, with the function only; the person at the other side is not kept.

Tables: `relations`, `relation_links` (replaced whole on every run), and `relation_tags` (what the workshop notes; never touched by the sync and never written back). Scheduled daily at 05:50, after the reference sync. A relation that leaves the address book is switched off, not deleted, so its tags stay.

## The page

- **Netwerk**: each relation a dot, larger for more projects; a line between two relations that stood on the same projects, thicker for more. Coloured by role (client, supplier, contact) or by the group given at the table, with a red ring for high importance. Choose how many relations (30 to 150) and from how many shared projects a line is drawn. Relations without such a line sit in a row underneath. Tap a dot to open it. The layout is a small force layout in `resources/js/network-graph.js`, with no new package and nothing new for the content policy.
- **Contacten**: the table with role, projects, group, importance, carrier and last date, filtered by role, group or words.
- **Nieuw en stil**: relations created in Bouwsoft during the period, and relations with at least two projects but none in the last twelve months.
- **Van offerte tot order**: quotes and orders accepted, rejected and still open, per month (per quarter over two or three years), per document type, the median days to a decision, and who asked most. Bouwsoft does not say through which channel a request came in, and the page says so.
- **The open relation**: its place, Bouwsoft group and since when, its projects with role and cost category, the relations it most often shares projects with, and the workshop form: group (the eight groups of the questionnaire), importance for the coming five years (hoog, midden, laag), who carries it today (only the owner, the owner with someone, someone else), and a note. The owner's name comes from `NETWORK_OWNER` (default Geert), not from code.
- **CSV met notities**: every relation of the period with its projects, dates and everything noted, for after the workshop.

## Who can see and tag

The same door as Verkennen: an office login, or a shared link that is still good. A link now opens Verkennen and Netwerk, with a two-item menu, and its holder may tag, because tagging is what the facilitators do at the table. Who saved a tag is kept (office user or link name).

## Tests

`NetworkTest` (10): the sync keeps names, roles, projects and dates and no amounts; a second sync replaces links and keeps tags; projects counted per relation and an undated project contact counted through its project; the graph's shared projects; new and stalled relations; acquisition totals and median; every tab and saving a tag; a shared link can open and tag; strangers are sent to the login; the CSV carries the notes. Full suite 226/226, pint clean. Checked in a browser against a local database with a made-up network of 33 relations and 140 projects: the graph, opening and tagging a relation, every tab.

## After merge

The deploy runs the migration. Then, once, on the server, so the page is filled before the workshop rather than at 05:50:

    php artisan relations:sync

It prints the counts per source. Bouwsoft's field values (the approved flag, how `groups` comes back) are read as the field list suggests but are untested on real rows; if a count looks wrong, the page and that output show it first.
params.title: Netwerk: GLK's relations from Bouwsoft as a graph, tagged at the workshop, and quote to order
